title: Lattice theme manifest
description: Per-theme IDENTITY and SCOPE. Deliberately carries NO token names and NO token values: those live in the CSS, and duplicating them here is the drift surface that sank every earlier manifest proposal (see engineering/decisions/2026-08-09-theme-token-contract.md). The rule is: the manifest owns SCOPE (which themes a rule applies to), the code owns CONTRACT (what the rule requires). Every field is either impossible to state in CSS, or gated against the CSS by tools/check-ownership.js.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema, for editor completion.

name.description: The palette slug. MUST equal the filename stem — a deck's `theme:` resolves to `themes/<name>.css`, so this is the same identifier the engine reads. Gated (G1).

role.description: What kind of theme file this is. `base` @imports 'lattice' and declares the full token contract. `variant-dark` @imports a base and declares no tokens of its own — it only pins the canvas. `derived-variant` @imports another theme and overrides a subset. This is the field the repo previously inferred three different, non-nested ways (listBasePalettes / checkCatInkDeclared / derive-cat-ink), which is why `carta` fell out of two gates entirely. Gated against the file's own imports and token count (G2).

extends.description: The theme this one @imports. Required unless role is `base` (which imports the engine, not a theme). Gated against the actual @import (G2).

family.description: Taxonomy, not derivable from the CSS. `brand` palettes carry a curated identity; `a11y` palettes exist to solve a color-vision constraint and are held to different distinctness rules.

tier.description: Which group the palette picker lists this under. Required for `base` themes, meaningless for the others. Previously hand-maintained in docs/src/components/studio/palettes.ts as CURATED / MORE_THEMES.

modes.description: The canvases this palette declares a DISTINCT face for. A palette whose surface tokens are `light-dark(L, D)` with L !== D has both. One that pins its own `color-scheme` at `:root` narrows to that face; one whose surface tokens are static — carbone opts out of `light-dark()` entirely — has only the face its zero-specificity default names. This is what makes carbone's dark-only-ness an asserted, checkable fact instead of a comment (#1302). Gated against the CSS (G3).

darkCounterpart.description: The `variant-dark` theme that pins this palette's dark face, or null when it has none. Required for `base` themes. Replaces the implicit `<name>-dark` filename convention with a declaration a gate can check (G3).

order.description: Position within this theme's picker group. Curated, not derivable — the brand group deliberately leads with indaco rather than sorting alphabetically. Required for every theme the picker lists, and must be unique within a group.

swatch.description: The dot the palette picker shows next to this theme. Curated menu data, not derivable from the palette (it is not simply --accent). Previously hand-maintained in ThemePicker's PALETTE_DOTS. Required for every theme the picker lists (role `base`, or any theme declaring `cvd`).

cvd.description: The color-vision deficiency this palette is designed for. Only meaningful in the `a11y` family, and impossible to state in CSS.

note.description: One line, for a deliberate oddity a reader would otherwise mistake for an omission. This is the field #1302 asked for.
